newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa due higher, faces big hurdle.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa due higher, faces big hurdle.

text.p: MAY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
LIFFE cocoa coffee are due to gap 25-30 stg higher at the open on Wednesday based on sharply higher New York values on Tuesday, traders said.
On the charts the market faced stiff resistance around 1,040 stg a tonne, the last peaks seen in late March, so additional gains might prove difficult.
New York cocoa futures jumped on Tuesday to their highest level since July 1994 as speculators bought heavily amid bullish technical indicators and sterling strength.
"There was no news and no selling," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "Once the market got over the psychologically important level of $1,500 (a tonne basis May), it just took off."

Most-active May gained $59 a tonne on the day -- about four percent -- to $1,512, after ranging from $1,520 to $1,440. Second-month July, which peaked at a new life-of-contract high of $1,547, rose $58 to $1,540.
Broker GNI said the close above $1,500 suggested a move to $1,580, then $1,828.
In London, analysts said the market had been ranging sideways but there was nothing to show that it was consolidating its recent gains.
Resistance is just at above 1,040 stg, the top of the range.
"If it goes up, there's a lot of supply above it which is going to make additional gains difficult," Susan Rigg of Chart Analysis said.
"It is more likely to extend the range at the present time because the May-August 1996 trading we have above it is likely to cap rises in the short term," she added.
Cocoa last peaked at 1,074 stg in August.
On the downside, support is seen safe above 997.
